bayts.text: Muḥammad: his remembrance is my intimacy and my joy, the light of my heart, of my limbs and of my repose.
He is my hope in the two Abodes: he is present with me at my death-throes, in my grave and at the Resurrections.
He is the Intercessor by whose rank the Forgiver (Al-Ghaffār) forgives me every disobedience and slip.
He is the sincere counsellor by whose rank the All-Merciful (Ar-Raḥmān) is gentle with me and guards me from delusions.
He is the one who joins, by whose rank my Lord brings me (to Him) and guards me from veils.
He is the generous one by whose rank the Maker (Al-Bāriʾ) honours me and guards me from humiliations.
He is the guarantor by whose rank the Bountiful (Al-Mannān) makes me happy and guards me from miseries.
He is the lofty one by whose rank the Most Tender (Al-Ḥannān) raises me and entrusts me with acts of worship.
He is the strong one by whose rank the Most High supports me and guards me from snares.
He is the bringer of glad tidings by whose rank the Guide (Al-Hādī) gives me glad tidings and guards me from every grief.
He is the one by whose rank the Benign (Al-Barr) protects me, guards me and shields me from harms.
He is the bountiful one by whose rank the Provider (Ar-Razzāq) provides for me and shields me from disgraces.
He is the intimate confidant by whose rank the Patron (Al-Wālī) teaches me, from Himself, hidden secrets.
He is the educator who without doubt turns me away from all obstacles and from vices.
He is the one who raises up, who without doubt casts upon me, for ever, a glance of purification from calamities.
He is the generous one whose gifts have been sublime with me, and he has led my reins at every hour.
For this reason I have bound myself to him, every year, to the debt of praise in rare verses.
I have indeed bound myself to him, every year, as long as my reason remains with me, to the debt of gifts.
And how could I leave off for a year the thanks owed to an intermediary, the loftiest of all intermediaries and means of approach?
Every year his gifts reach me; nay, at every moment he consoles me with favours.
Light is his tomb, an ocean is his genius; his sincere counsel has embraced all creatures.
He is the refuge in which the noble have taken refuge, when they understood that he is the one who relieves complaints.
And there has been no chief who attained a rank, but that he sought access (to Allah) through him, at some moment among moments.
His excellent forefathers sought access (to Allah) through him, and through him obtained from Allah the triumph of answered prayers.
They all obtained through him, before (his) birth, whatever they sought through him of weighty affairs and needs.
By his rank Adam won forgiveness, after the descent from rivers and gardens.
Through him Allah saved Noah (Nūḥ) in his ark, and his rank warded off misfortunes from Jacob (Yaʿqūb).
Through the Chosen One (Muḥammad) the Bountiful (Al-Mannān) brought Joseph (Yūsuf) out of a strong prison and out of those depths (of the well).
And the Companion of the Fish (Jonah, Yūnus) took refuge with the Lord and was saved through the Select One (Muḥammad), and drew far from every anguish.
Through him the fire of Abraham (Ibrāhīm) became coolness and safety (Qurʾān 21:69): and this is a wonder breaking the customary order.
Like the cleaving of Sinimmār's (palace) at his appearing; and the lizard one day addressed him with words.
And the (palm) trunk moaned out of longing and out of sorrow, with the moan of a bereaved mother grieved by the loss of her dead.
Among the wonders: the hastening march of the trees (toward him); and the wolf one day spoke to him with its voice.
Among them, by my life, is the Night Journey (Isrāʾ) on which God took him, in spirit and in body, by night, to the heavens.
He spent the night journeying, and Gabriel (Jibrīl) journeyed with him, upon al-Burāq, to the farthest of limits.
And the prophets and all the messengers together learned from him the proprieties of worship.
He attained what he attained of a secret reserved for him alone, and he drew near and came down nearer still (Qurʾān 53:8) in intimate converse.
And (Allah) singled him out with that which no one has ever been granted, nor shall be granted to any of the past or of the future.
He returned in the night, before dawn, to make known what in the Law is negation or affirmation.
Those wonders never ceased to support him, for his intimate Friend (Gabriel) never ceased to bring signs.
Until he brought a Book that left the eloquent powerless, and the masters of fluency fell short of producing its like.
How noble a Book it is! It has healed ailments and rescued all the Companions from dullness.
It is the Book in which there is no doubt (Qurʾān 2:2), a guidance for whoever guards himself against the Fire through acts of obedience.
It is the guidance and the straight path for us: whoever has spurned it has met with miseries.
It is the cure for all who suffer from a malady; it saves those endowed with reason from error and calamities.
And whoever seeks a bond with Allah while turning away from it, the rope of union has already escaped him.
It is the path in which there is no crookedness, for whoever journeys toward the Giver of desired goods (Allah).
Command and prohibition, promise and threat together have been set down in it, as guidance toward good deeds.
Whoever perseveres in its service, seeking the Face of Allah, shall surely be favoured with gifts.
And whoever at all times holds fast to it, that one is among the people of sainthood.
For it is the firmest handhold (Qurʾān 2:256): whoever grasps it shall tomorrow win Gardens with the Lord.
And to whoever clings to it in his worldly life, it shall grant on the Day of Resurrection glad tidings and blessedness.
And whoever clings to it, ever reciting its text with reflection, shall attain sublime things.
And whoever turns aside from it in his hours, keeping apart, it is the multitude of vices that has turned him away.
There have turned him from it things that number up to seven vices, insidious calamities:
sin, pride, persistence in (frivolous) play, love of the world, reliance upon creatures;
likewise weakness of certainty, which is the sixth; and they have made them seven with the multiplying of innovations.
How excellent is he who brought it to us from the Possessor of Majesty (Dhū l-Jalāl), and led us from delusion to the virtues!
He is our refuge in this world and the Hereafter, in every calamity, here or in the morrow to come.
Saviour, protector, intercessor, helper and bulwark: he wards off from us trials and misfortunes.
So I entrust my affair, here and tomorrow, to none but him, after my Lord, Lord of creatures.
O noblest of creation, I am your servant, as long as I live, through praise and through defence by means of poems.
And I have not sought the flower of the world which the hands of Zuhayr (ibn Abī Sulmā) plucked for the verses of praise he composed.
Rather I have praised you, O my master, seeking from you good pleasure, after you have erased my sins.
Upon you, the Family and the Companions be the best blessing with peace, through which I attain distinctions.
